 We predict the winner of Survivor 51 based on the merged tribe dynamics
 Jacqueline Thomas Wed, November 11, 2026 at 4:26 AM UTC 5 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. "The Girl at the Prom" - It's time to "Drop Your Buffs!". The castaways face a daunting rite of passage that harkens all the way back to season one. Then, chaos ensues as the group mingles and navigates old alliances and new promises while battling for the first individual immunity necklace of the season, on SURVIVOR, Wednesday, Nov. 4 (8:00-9:30 PM, ET/PT) Photo: Robert Voets/CBS 2026 CBS Broadcasting, Inc. All Rights Reserved. | Robert Voets/CBS Fans of Survivor know that the merge is the beginning of the end, but the game is far from over. All the relationships made and moves executed pre-merge are now transitioning from outlast-tactics to resume-builders, amplifying the threat of every single thing each of our twelve remaining castaways does in the game.
 But Survivor 51 , of course, has been different. It's the open era and anything can happen at any time to shake up the game.
 The latest "Next Time on Survivor " preview has shown us that we are getting a Dynamic Duos twist in episode 8, but we don't know exactly how the twist will impact the game. Will it be a copy & paste of Survivor 50 where two players' lives are connected and they must win together or potentially get eliminated together?
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement I think it feels a little soon to implement a twist that was so gamechanging, again, but, like I said, it's the open era. I wouldn't put it past host and showrunner Jeff Probst to have some moments exemplify the most amount of chaos as possible at this critical interval in the season.
 And while this next episode has the potential to blow-up the game for real, there are still a few people that regardless of their partner in the challenge, have the social gameplay power to outlast the rest.
 The three players most likely to win Survivor 51 after the merge are Sharonda Cox, Angelica "Jelly" Loblack, and Devin Way.
 The Helicopter Alliance may just come out on top, y'all! While I don't necessarily think it's possible for these three players to be our Final Three at the end of the day-I think Jelly and Devin will have to turn on each other at some point...-I do believe one of these castaways has what it takes to win it all.
 Let's take a look at their games!
 "Weaponized Honesty" - A chilling injury at camp threatens to send one player home. Two tribes face off in a daunting immunity challenge at sea where one tribe struggles to keep afloat. Then, tribal council takes a wild turn when one player attempts a never-before-seen move to save an ally, on SURVIVOR, Wednesday, Sept. 30 (8:00-9:30 PM, ET/PT) on the CBS Television Network, and streaming on Paramount+. Photo: Scott Duncan/CBS 2026 CBS Broadcasting, Inc. All Rights Reserved. | Scott Duncan/CBS
 Sharonda Cox
 Sharonda is in the best position right now and is the only player who has truly stayed level-headed through every circumstance she's been thrown into. With an idol in her pocket that Kristin Flickinger has promised to play for her (knowing she can only play it for her) if she needs it, Sharonda has already put in the work and built the relationships that she needs to get to the end of the game.
 "Permanent Uncertainty" - Castaways marooned in remote Fiji embark upon the Open Era of SURVIVOR and battle to win $1 million. The catchphrase of the season, "permanent uncertainty," comes into play as soon as the cast"Permanent Uncertainty" - Castaways marooned in remote Fiji embark upon the Open Era of SURVIVOR and battle to win $1 million on the two-hour 51st season premiere of SURVIVOR, Wednesday, Sept. 23. Photo: Scott Duncan/CBS 2026 CBS Broadcasting, Inc. All Rights Reserved. | Scott Duncan/CBS
 Jelly Loblack
 While the beginning of the game was a little rocky for Jelly, she's managed to turn it around and ended up on the right side of the first vote after the merge. She also has an idol in her pocket-one that can keep her or an ally safe-that no one except Devin knows about. While he could potentially blow up her game with it, it's more likely he'll want to stay loyal for a while to keep the momentum going of being a solid ally for others. This will benefit Jelly in the end and likely allow her to take out Devin before Devin takes her out.
 Survivor. - "What I'm Smellin' Is Stinky." Pictured: Devin Way | Robert Voets/CBS
 Devin Way
 There is no doubt that Devin is one of-if not the -most charming players this season. Despite the fact that he's been a little bit of a bully this season, there's still time to turn things around and lay low now that the merge has hit. I think if he keeps to the shadows and plays his cards right, there is a very high potential he's sitting at the end with the assumption that none of the jury will vote for him based on his early game. But if he can slip through the cracks and play the right kind of end game, he could get the votes to become the Sole Survivor.
